biography: Tim Tudor, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in the paddocks, hails from a small village in Oxfordshire. His racing journey began not on asphalt, but on the muddy fields of his family's farm, where he'd tear around on an old tractor, much to the chagrin of his father. At 16, he entered a local karting competition, winning by a landslide, showcasing an innate ability to control speed. This initial triumph spurred him to pursue racing professionally, starting with Formula Ford and steadily climbing the ladder. A defining moment came at the Brands Hatch Grand Prix in 2018 where, despite starting in last place due to a mechanical issue, he carved his way through the pack, ultimately securing a podium finish. Currently, at 36, Tudor finds himself at what many consider his peak, racing for MCR S2000. Though consistent results elude him, flashes of brilliance remind everyone of his potential. He's a driver who can either win you the race or crash out on the first lap, a frustratingly unpredictable talent.
drivingStyle: Tudor's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the car right to the edge of grip. He tends to overdrive the car, particularly under pressure, which leads to spectacular overtakes and equally spectacular crashes. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers extracting maximum performance from the tires early in the stint, often sacrificing longevity for immediate gains. This aggressive approach has earned him both victories and DNFs in equal measure, solidifying his reputation as one of the more thrilling drivers to watch, even if he is prone to the occasional mistake.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Montoya
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at Monza in 2021, resulting in Montoya losing the championship lead.

rivalries.name: Anika Schmidt
rivalries.reason: A constant battle for track position, with both drivers known for their uncompromising racing styles.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A personality clash, with Dubois often criticizing Tudor's inconsistent performance and perceived arrogance.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, even if they're full of holes.
Before each race, he meticulously polishes his helmet visor with a microfiber cloth, regardless of the weather.
He refuses to eat anything green on race weekends, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. If you ain't spinning, you ain't winning!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Silverstone Grand Prix in 2020, overcoming a mid-race puncture to take the victory in front of his home crowd.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Monaco Grand Prix in 2022, costing him a potential championship-defining win.
